arxiv-2010-09072.title: UoB at SemEval-2020 Task 1: Automatic Identification of Novel Word Senses
arxiv-2010-09072.creator: Eleri Sarsfield, Harish Tayyar Madabushi
arxiv-2010-09072.description: Abstract Much as the social landscape in which languages are spoken shifts, language too evolves to suit the needs of its users. Lexical semantic change analysis is a burgeoning field of semantic analysis which aims to trace changes in the meanings of words over time.

arxiv-2401-14199.title: MTRGL: Effective Temporal Correlation Discerning through Multi-modal Temporal Relational Graph Learning
arxiv-2401-14199.creator: Junwei Su, Shan Wu, Jinhui Li
arxiv-2401-14199.description: Abstract In this study, we explore the synergy of deep learning and financial market applications, focusing on pair trading. This market-neutral strategy is integral to quantitative finance and is apt for advanced deep-learning techniques. A pivotal challenge in pair trading is discerning temporal correlations among entities, necessitating the integration of diverse data modalities.

arxiv-2401-17442.title: Detection of Signals in Colored Noise: Leading Eigenvalue Test for Non-central F F -matrices
arxiv-2401-17442.creator: Prathapasinghe Dharmawansa 1 , Saman Atapattu 2 , Jamie Evans 1 , and Kandeepan Sithamparanathan 2
arxiv-2401-17442.description: Abstract This paper investigates the signal detection problem in colored noise with an unknown covariance matrix. In particular, we focus on detecting an unknown non-random signal by capitalizing on the leading eigenvalue of the whitened sample covariance matrix as the test statistic (a.k.a. Roy’s largest root test).

arxiv-2402-14071.title: Altermagnetic superconducting diode effect
arxiv-2402-14071.creator: Sayan Banerjee, Mathias S. Scheurer
arxiv-2402-14071.description: A 2024 arXiv research paper by Sayan Banerjee, Mathias S. Scheurer. Non-reciprocal superconductivity, also known as the superconducting diode effect, has been extensively studied in the presence of a magnetic field or some form of ferromagnetic order breaking time-reversal symmetry. We here show that another class of magnetic order known as altermagnetism, which also breaks time-reversal symmetry but does not exhibit a finite net magnetic moment, can also give rise to a superconducting diode effect.

arxiv-2412-06541.title: Numerical Estimation of Spatial Distributions under Differential Privacy Thanks: *Wangze Ni is also with The State Key Laboratory of Blockchain and Data Security; Hangzhou High-Tech Zone (Binjiang) Institute of Blockchain and Data Security.
arxiv-2412-06541.creator: Leilei Du , Peng Cheng , Libin Zheng , Xiang Lian , Lei Chen , Wei Xi , Wangze Ni, East China Normal University, China; Sun Yat-sen University, China; Kent State University, USA
arxiv-2412-06541.description: Abstract Estimating spatial distributions is important in data analysis, such as traffic flow forecasting and epidemic prevention. To achieve accurate spatial distribution estimation, the analysis needs to collect sufficient user data. However, collecting data directly from individuals could compromise their privacy.

arxiv-2412-08675.title: Metric Field as Emergence of Hilbert Space
arxiv-2412-08675.creator: Maysam Yousefian, Mehrdad Farhoudi
arxiv-2412-08675.description: Abstract First, we explain some ambiguities of spacetime and metric field as fundamental concepts. Then, from the Unruh effect point of view and using the Gelfand-Naimark-Segal construction, we construct an operator as a quanta of acceleration that we call quantum acceleration operator (QAO). Thereupon, we investigate the relation between the vacuum of two different frames in the Minkowski space.

arxiv-2508-00396.title: Proof complexity of Mal’tsev CSP
arxiv-2508-00396.creator: Azza Gaysin
arxiv-2508-00396.description: Abstract Constraint Satisfaction Problems (CSPs) form a broad class of combinatorial problems, which can be formulated as homomorphism problems between relational structures. The CSP dichotomy theorem classifies all such problems over finite domains into two categories: NP-complete and polynomial-time [ 9 ] , [ 20 ] . Polynomial-time CSPs can be further subdivided into smaller subclasses.

arxiv-2508-07102.title: Towards High-Order Mean Flow Generative Models: Feasibility, Expressivity, and Provably Efficient Criteria
arxiv-2508-07102.creator: Yang Cao and Yubin Chen and Zhao Song and Jiahao Zhang
arxiv-2508-07102.description: Abstract Generative modelling has seen significant advances through simulation-free paradigms such as Flow Matching, and in particular, the 𝖬𝖾𝖺𝗇𝖥𝗅𝗈𝗐 \mathsf{MeanFlow} framework, which replaces instantaneous velocity fields with average velocities to enable efficient single-step sampling. In this work, we introduce a theoretical study on Second-Order 𝖬𝖾𝖺𝗇𝖥𝗅𝗈𝗐 \mathsf{MeanFlow} , a novel extension that incorporates average acceleration fields into the 𝖬𝖾𝖺𝗇𝖥𝗅𝗈𝗐 \mathsf{MeanFlow} objective.

arxiv-2509-15571.title: Uniform Sampling from the Reachable Set Using Optimal Transport
arxiv-2509-15571.creator: Karthik Elamvazhuthi, Sachin Shivakumar
arxiv-2509-15571.description: A 2025 arXiv research paper by Karthik Elamvazhuthi, Sachin Shivakumar. Finding the reachable set of a system has a wide range of applications, but is a fundamental challenge in control theory, especially when controls are bounded. Although one can simply integrate the system samples forward in time by applying random admissible control to approximate the reachable set, the samples typically cluster near an attractor (if one is present) – yielding a poor representation of the reachable set.

arxiv-2510-05860.title: Automated Boilerplate: Prevalence and Quality of Contract Generators in the Context of Swiss Privacy Policies Conference: TBD; ;
arxiv-2510-05860.creator: Luka Nenadic, David Rodriguez
arxiv-2510-05860.description: Abstract Abstract It has become increasingly challenging for firms to comply with a plethora of novel digital regulations. This is especially true for smaller businesses that often lack both the resources and know-how to draft complex legal documents. Instead of seeking costly legal advice from attorneys, firms may turn to cheaper alternative legal service providers such as automated contract generators.

arxiv-2601-00071.title: Diagnosing Metal-Insulator and Hawking-Page Transitions: A Mixed-State Entanglement Perspective in Einstein-Born-Infeld-Massive Gravity
arxiv-2601-00071.creator: Zhe Yang 1,2, Jian-Pin Wu 1, Peng Liu 2
arxiv-2601-00071.description: Abstract We study mixed-state entanglement measures in Einstein-Born-Infeld (EN-BI) massive gravity theory, a model exhibiting both Hawking-Page transitions and metal-insulator transitions (MIT) at finite temperatures. Our comprehensive investigation reveals that the entanglement wedge cross-section (EWCS), a novel mixed-state entanglement measure, demonstrates unique properties in detecting phase transitions.

pmc-10693878.description: PurposeClinic-based or community-based interventions can improve adherence to guideline-directed medication therapies (GDMTs) among patients with heart failure (HF). However, opportunities for such interventions are frequently missed, as providers may be unable to recognise risk patterns for medication non-adherence. Machine learning algorithms can help in identifying patients with high likelihood of non-adherence.

pmc-11681494.title: Exploring the Impact of Hemoglobin on Cerebral Blood Flow in Arterial Territories and Surgical Outcomes: Potential Implications for Moyamoya Disease Treatment
pmc-11681494.creator: Xinfeng Yu, Duo Xu, Junwen Hu, Yannan Yu, Lin Wang, Biao Jiang, Minming Zhang
pmc-11681494.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2024). BackgroundChanges in levels of hemoglobin would result in alterations of cerebral blood flow (CBF). However, the impact of hemoglobin on CBF in moyamoya disease (MMD) remains largely unknown. This study sought to determine whether CBF would be influenced by hemoglobin before surgical revascularization and to analyze the relationships between hemoglobin and CBF with clinical outcome after surgery in patients with MMD.Methods and ResultsWe prospectively enrolled adult patients with MMD undergoing surgical revascularization between June 2020 and December 2022.

pmc-12404391.title: SEE+ computerized classroom-based training enhances 7- to 10-year-olds' socio-emotional cognition through observation and inference
pmc-12404391.creator: Sveta Mayer, Iroise Dumontheil, Hannah R. Wilkinson, Kaska Porayska-Pomsta, Emily K. Farran, Andrew K. Tolmie, Denis Mareschal, the UnLocke Team
pmc-12404391.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2025). Smooth social interactions rely on children’s abilities to decode others’ social signals, which includes what an individual may say or do, and their facial emotional expressions. Failure can lead to exclusion from social groups. Consequently, a number of social and emotional learning (SEL) training programmes have been developed, with some evidence of positive impacts on those skills themselves and on academic achievement.

pmc-12615001.title: Oxidative balance score and all-cause mortality among hypertensive individuals
pmc-12615001.creator: Lian-Zhen Huang, Hong-Bin Zhang, Mei Qin, Ze-Bin Ni, Wei-Feng Huang, Ji Li, Li-Ping Sheng, Li-Yun Guo, Jin-Yan Zhang
pmc-12615001.description: BackgroundOxidative stress contributes to hypertension and its complications. The oxidative balance score (OBS) could therefore provide insight into the relationship with mortality in hypertensive individuals. We aimed to investigate the association between OBS and all-cause mortality using data from National Health and Nutrition Examination Survey 2007–18.MethodsOur sample comprised 11 196 hypertensive participants.

pmc-13170394.description: Patient: Female, 37-year-old Final Diagnosis: Type A aortic dissection Symptoms: Sudden severe pain in both chest and back Clinical Procedure: — Specialty: Cardiac Surgery Objective: Rare coexistence of disease or pathology BackgroundType A aortic dissection during pregnancy, a rare and fatal clinical emergency, is highly challenging to the survival of both the mother and her fetus.

pmc-13408444.title: Ubiquitin-driven regulation of immune checkpoints in lung cancer: Mechanisms and therapeutic implications (Review)
pmc-13408444.creator: Lin Chai, Lin-Rong Pang, Yi-Ting Li, Jia-Hui Wang, Jun Chen, Zu-Guo Yuan, Xiao-Feng Jin
pmc-13408444.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2026). The ubiquitin-proteasome system is a master regulator of anti-tumor immunity in lung cancer, which primarily functions through controlling the stability of immune checkpoint proteins. The present review offers a synthesis concerning how a dynamic balance between E3 ubiquitin ligases (E3s) and deubiquitinases (DUBs) dictates the fate of key checkpoint proteins, including programmed cell death protein 1/programmed death-ligand 1, lymphocyte-activating gene 3 and B7 homolog 4.

pmc-13574246.title: Born This Way: Individuality Is Seeded Before Birth and Robust to Ecological Stress
pmc-13574246.creator: James H. Gallagher, Ammon D. Perkes, Chia‐Chen Chang, Emma S. Chirila, Karen Kacevas, Kate L. Laskowski
pmc-13574246.description: Behavioural individuality is widespread, yet its developmental origins are unclear. We subjected clonal individuals to a critical ecological challenge—the threat of predation—to disentangle the developmental mechanisms of individuality. Predation may erode or amplify among‐individual differences, demonstrating that individuality is developmentally plastic. If individuality is instead determined before birth, it should resist environmental influences.
